cartpreview.help_rom.text: Holds the game program, images, sounds and text. Progress is saved in a separate chip.

cartpreview.help_sram.text: Memory accessed directly for reads and writes. It is volatile: its contents are lost when power is removed.

cartpreview.help_eeprom.text: Retains progress without power. Communication uses a serial protocol, which requires a dedicated save driver.

cartpreview.help_flash.text: Retains saves without power. Before rewriting some areas, the game must erase blocks of memory.

cartpreview.help_fram.text: Ferroelectric memory that retains data without a battery. Access works like SRAM, without Flash-style erase sequences.

cartpreview.help_battery_save.text: Takes over when the console is off to keep SRAM powered. It does not power the game itself.

cartpreview.help_battery_rtc.text: Keeps the clock running when the console is off. A depleted battery does not erase saves in the Flash chip.

cartpreview.help_rtc.text: Tracks the real date and time, including between sessions with battery power. The game reads this information separately from saves.

uiinsp.priority.tip.text: Sets the depth when this element renders as a sprite, which happens when its node follows an actor. Auto inherits the depth of the actor, live.

uiinsp.text.content_tip.text: Without an entry, this text belongs to the element and appears when the scene starts. Create an entry to share or translate it in Texts.

uiinsp.text.page_add.text: Add a page to the sequence

uiinsp.text.page_remove.text: Delete the last page of the sequence

uiinsp.text.page_remove_msg.text: Delete the text “{page}” and its translations? Undo restores it.

uiinsp.text.page_drag.text: Drag to reorder pages (renames their keys)

txtseq.delete_sequence_tip.text: Delete the whole sequence, empty its table and its TextBox

txtpnl.delete_sequence_msg.text:
Delete “{name}”: its {n} texts and their translations?

Linked: {users}. The table is emptied and the TextBox is left empty. Undo restores everything.

uiinsp.text.sequence_free.text: Not linked to a text sequence

uiinsp.text.create_entry_tip.text: Open the Text editor to create a named, shared and translatable entry.

uiinsp.text.bank_tip.text: Sets the palette bank shared by every text of this scene. A background can pick its bank per element, but a text cannot: every text must agree on the same bank.

uiinsp.text.ink_tip.text: Sets the color of the glyphs, as an index in the UI palette bank of the scene. Font ink keeps the shades of the font (outline, fill); any other value flattens the ink to that single color.

uiinsp.text.highlight_tip.text: Lays a color under the text, on the tiles it actually covers. By default a text sits on the background of its container; a highlight overrides it, marker-style, on the written extent only.

uiinsp.fill.sprite_tip.text: Tiles a sprite across the panel. Unlike an image, the panel keeps its own size: the sprite repeats to cover it.

uiinsp.fill.state_tip.text: Sets the initial animation state. A panel background gets an IMAGE_* constant of its own, like any image.

uiinsp.fill.speed_tip.text: Sets the frames between two animation frames, overriding the speed of the state. 0 (= From sprite) keeps the value edited in the Sprite Editor.

uiinsp.list.selection_tip.text: Sets whether this list reads the D-pad. An inactive list stays on screen and keeps its current item; it just stops moving.

uiinsp.list.columns_tip.text: Sets how wide one line of the grid is. One column is a plain vertical list; the number of rows gives a row of tabs, and any other width gives a grid.

uiinsp.list.order_tip.text: Sets the direction in which item numbers run. Column first goes top to bottom, then to the next column; row first goes left to right, then to the line below.

uiinsp.list.ink_tip.text: Sets the ink of the selected row, as an index in the UI palette bank of the scene, like the own ink of a text. The default keeps whatever each row already uses.

uiinsp.list.highlight_tip.text: Lays a color under the text of the selected row, on the extent it covers. It is the classic way to mark a menu selection without a cursor.

uiinsp.img.sprite_tip.text: Picks the sprite asset drawn here. Picking one resizes the element to its frame.

uiinsp.img.state_tip.text: Sets the state shown when the scene starts.

uiinsp.img.play_tip.text: A frozen image costs no per-frame work and never rewrites the tilemap. It is the right default for a static HUD icon.

uiinsp.bank_inherited_tip.text: This text sits in a filled container, so it reads its ink from the bank of the container.

comped.interact_input_tip.text: The gesture on the built-in "interact" input (Project Settings > Input) that triggers on_interact. Pressed fires on the frame the input goes down, Held once it has been down for the set number of frames, Released when it comes up while the actor is still in the zone.

comped.interact_hold_frames_tip.text: Frames the input must stay down inside the zone.

comped.interact_area_tip.text: How the player reaches the zone. Hover: the player overlaps it. Facing: the player's box, projected in the direction it looks over the reach set in the project settings and stopped by walls, touches it.

comped.interact_box_tip.text: Where the zone comes from. The own box is created by the component, with the reserved collision tag; or an existing collision box of this actor, chosen by its tag.

comped.interact_size_tip.text: Size of the own box in pixels. Auto uses the sprite frame, or 16 x 16 without a sprite.

projset.reserved_tag_tip.text: The editor relies on this tag (Player, Interactive): it cannot be renamed or removed. Its matrix cells stay editable.

actorinsp.empty.text:
Select an actor
from the left panel

actorinsp.sprite_preview_tip.text: A click assigns a sprite from the project. The first frame of the initial state is shown.

actorinsp.rel.parent_tip.text: Opens the parent of this element.

actorinsp.children_tip.text: The children of this element. For a prefab, its parts, such as the segments of a boss: each part is a full actor with its own sprite, boxes and local transform.

actorinsp.children_note.text: A double-click opens a child; dragging a prefab part onto another one reparents it. The pool reserves max instances × (1 + parts) entries.

actorinsp.index_tip.text: Position of the actor in the scene. It sets the processing and render order.

actorinsp.relink_tip.text: Reloads the components, palette and notes from the current definition of the prefab.

actorinsp.expose_tip.text: Pushes the components, palette and notes of this instance up to the prefab.

actorinsp.expose_new_tip.text: Creates a prefab from the components, palette and notes of this actor. This actor becomes its first linked instance.

actorinsp.parent_tip.text: Expresses the position of this actor in the frame of its parent. X/Y, rotation and scale become local, and the subtree of the parent follows it. Hiding the parent hides its whole subtree.

actorinsp.is_player_tip.text: Marks this actor as the one that interacts: only an actor with this tag triggers the Interactive components of the scene. It is an actor tag, not a collision tag. Several actors may carry it.

sceneinsp.notes_tip.text: Holds editor notes for this scene. They are not shown in the game.

sceneinsp.no_scene_prefab.text: No prefab is placed or spawned

sceneinsp.mode_not_impl_note.text: This mode is not available in the editor yet.

sceneinsp.mode_tip_0.text: Provides 4 regular tiled backgrounds (BG0 to BG3), in 4 or 8 bpp.

sceneinsp.mode_tip_1.text: Provides regular BG0 and BG1, with an affine BG2 for rotation and scale.

sceneinsp.mode_tip_3.text: Provides a BG2 bitmap in 16 bpp direct color, 240 × 160, without palette.

sceneinsp.mode_tip_4.text: Provides a BG2 bitmap with an 8 bpp palette, 256 colors, 240 × 160.

sceneinsp.mode_tip_5.text: Provides a BG2 bitmap in 16 bpp direct color, 160 × 128.

sceneinsp.backdrop_tip.text: Chooses the color shown where no background layer or sprite is drawn.

sceneinsp.backdrop_note.text: The value is quantized to the GBA's BGR555 color format.

sceneinsp.backdrop_reset_tip.text: Reuses the backdrop color defined at project level.

sceneinsp.transition_tip.text: Chooses the fade played when this scene opens and when it closes.

sceneinsp.transition_frames_tip.text: Sets the duration of each half of the transition: leaving, then opening.

sceneinsp.music_tip.text: Chooses a track, keeps the current music, or explicitly switches to silence.

sceneinsp.music_note.text: A scene-start script can replace this choice.

sceneinsp.no_bitmap_text.text: Import an image in Bitmap mode first, in the Background Editor.

sceneinsp.ui_colors_tip.text: Chooses the scene background palette used by the default interface font.

sceneinsp.ui_font_tip.text: Chooses the font used by interface text when no font is specified.

sndmix.matrix_hint.text: An animation frame cites an action; the active state says which {kind} it points to. A cell left at “none” plays nothing in that state: a footstep does not sound mid-air.

sndmix.matrix_hint_empty.text: No action yet. Adding one, then dropping its name on a frame in the Sprite Editor, makes the same walk cycle usable on several grounds.

sndmix.new_action_prompt.text: Name (the one the frames will carry):

sndmix.auto_layout_tip.text: Arranges the nodes in columns starting from the start state.

sndmix.graph_hint_empty.text: No music state. '+ State' creates one.

sndmix.graph_hint_no_trans.text: Dragging the dot on the right edge of a node to another node creates a transition; clicking a wire then pressing Del cuts it.

sndmix.trigger_tip.text: Takes the name emitted by a script to run this transition.

sndmix.kind_tip.text: A fade crossfades two tracks. A cut keeps the playback position but requires matching track structures.

sndmix.frames_tip.text: Sets the fade duration in frames. The game runs at 60 frames per second.

sndmix.start_state_tip.text: Makes this the state active when the game starts. Only one state can be selected.

sndmix.intensity_tip.text: Chooses whether intensity controls the track volume, tempo or pitch.

sndmix.ivalue_tip.text: 100 % is neutral. Tempo and pitch are limited to 50–200 %.

edgeinsp.target_missing.text: Target « {target} » not found in the project

edgeinsp.notes_multi_placeholder.text: Note applied to all selected transitions…

bgedit.kind_scene_tip.text: Places this image as a layer in a scene. Its palette can be repainted tile by tile.

bgedit.kind_ui_tip.text: Uses this image in an interface panel, as a stretchable frame or a plain image.

bgedit.kind_animated_tip.text: Cuts this sheet into frames that can be placed and played on another background.

bgedit.tiled_tip.text: Builds a tilemap. Supports scrolling, tile reuse and palette repainting.

bgedit.bitmap_tip.text: Uses one full-screen image up to 240×160 pixels. Best for photos and title screens; tiles cannot be edited.

bgedit.d4_tip.text: Uses up to 16 colors per tile across 16 palettes. Supports palette repainting and tiled backgrounds.

bgedit.d8_tip.text: Uses one palette of up to 256 colors. Suitable for detailed pixel art and Mode 4 bitmaps.

bgedit.d16_tip.text: Direct 16bpp color is not available yet. Images with more than 256 colors are imported as a Mode 4 palettized bitmap.

bgedit.dithering_tip.text: Mixes nearby pixels to preserve gradients when colors are reduced. It can make crisp pixel art look softer.

bgedit.nine_tip.text: Keeps the corners and repeats the edges and the center when resized.

bgedit.plain_tip.text: Places the image at the top left and crops it to the size of the panel.

bgedit.margin_tip.text: Sets the fixed border on this side of a nine-slice frame, in pixels.

bgedit.margin_tip_note.text: The value is rounded down to an 8-pixel tile at build time.

bgedit.frame_tip.text: Sets the size of one animation frame in pixels. Full uses the whole image on this axis.

bgedit.speed_tip.text: Sets the number of ticks between two frames. A tick lasts 1/60 of a second, as for a sprite animation.

bgedit.per_instance_tip.text: Each copy placed on a background animates on its own.

bgedit.shared_tip.text: Every copy animates together, in step.

bgedit.src_hint.text: Dragging onto the canvas places it.

bgedit.anim_source_tip.singular: {n} frame. Dragging the animation onto the canvas places it.
bgedit.anim_source_tip.plural: {n} frames. Dragging the animation onto the canvas places it.

bgedit.pl_start_tip.text: Sets the frame on which this copy starts. Two copies of the same animation can thus be offset in the loop.

bgedit.pl_speed_tip.text: Sets the number of ticks between two frames for this copy only. The default value follows the speed of the animation.

bgedit.import_replace_tip.text: Imports a PNG and attaches it to this background. The source image file is not modified.

bgedit.restore_tip.text: Restores the background to its first import and recompresses the source PNG.

bgedit.restore_tip_warning.text: Added palettes and painting will be lost.

bgedit.extract_tip.text: Creates shared catalog palettes from the PNG and assigns them to this background. They stay editable in the Palette Editor.

bgedit.extract_warning.text: If these palettes already exist, their colors are replaced.

bgedit.limit_text.text: A background can only have 16 palettes.

bgedit.del_pal_text.text:
Remove palette {idx}?
Tiles using it will fall back to palette 0.

bgedit.restore_dialog_text.text:
Reset this background to its very first import?
Added palettes and painting (inpainting) will be lost.

bgedit.restore_no_png_text.text: Source PNG not found. Restoration impossible.

bgedit.no_extract_text.text: This background doesn't have a palette to extract yet (uncompressed or unreadable image).

sndpanel.rate_tip.text: Sets the sample rate used when this effect is built. The source file is not modified.

sndpanel.policy_tip.text: What happens to the music while this jingle plays. Keeps playing: nothing changes. Lowered: the music drops at once, then climbs back when the jingle ends. Paused: the music waits and resumes where it stopped.

sndpanel.duck_level_tip.text: The music's volume while the jingle plays, as a percentage of its own volume. Only used when the music is lowered.

sndpanel.duck_release_tip.text: How many frames the music takes to climb back to its volume once the jingle ends (60 per second). Zero brings it back at once. Only used when the music is lowered.

sndpanel.sfx_protected_tip.text: Keeps the effect's channel until its sample ends, even when every channel of the project is busy. An unprotected effect can lose its channel to a newer one; the weakest is the first to give way. Protected effects use up channels that the music and other effects can no longer take.

sndpanel.box_tip.text: Chooses the box to edit in this family. The game uses the first box by name.

sndpanel.right_empty.text:
Select or create
an SFX or a track
to edit its properties

sndpanel.rom_play_tip.text: Simulates the MusicBox with the same states and transitions as the game.

sndpanel.rom_play_note.text: Clicking a node emits the trigger that leads to it; if no edge leads to that node, nothing happens. This preview does not run a compiled ROM.

sndpanel.musicbox_empty.text: A MusicBox arranges musical states and the transitions between them: which track in which mood, and by which trigger the game moves from one to another.

sndpanel.soundbox_empty.text: A SoundBox says which effect each action points to per state. The same walk cycle sounds sand or gravel without being authored twice.

sndpanel.jinglebox_empty.text: A JingleBox says which module each jingle action points to per state. A jingle layers over the music, it doesn't replace it.

sndpanel.context_music_tip.text: Edits the MusicBoxes and their states.

sndpanel.context_sfx_tip.text: Edits the SoundBoxes and their actions.

sndpanel.context_jingles_tip.text: Edits the JingleBoxes and their actions.

sprframe.add_frame_tip.text: Adds a new frame after the current one. It duplicates the selected frame, or creates an empty frame.

sprframe.frame_tip.text: A click edits this frame, dragging it changes its order, and a right-click opens the frame actions and triggers.

sprframe.play_preview_tip.text: Plays the frames of the current direction at the animation speed.

sprframe.grid_tip.text: Shows the 8×8 pixel GBA tile grid on the frame canvas.

sprpanel.frame_size_tip.text: Defines the pixel area used to compose each animation frame.

sprpanel.speed_tip.text: Sets the number of GBA ticks between two frames. A tick lasts 1/60 of a second: 8 = 7.5 fps, 4 = 15 fps, 2 = 30 fps.

sprpanel.loop_tip.text: Loops the animation: when it reaches the last frame, it starts again.

sprpanel.import_replace_tip.text: Chooses an image, validates it and encodes it for the GBA, then attaches it to the current sprite. The source file is not modified.

sprpanel.extract_created.text: Palette “{name}” created from the image. It is in the Palettes screen.

sprpanel.extract_updated.text: Palette “{name}” updated from the image. It is in the Palettes screen.

sprpanel.extract_no_image.text: This sprite has no image file to read a palette from.

sprpanel.extract_tip.text: Creates a palette in the catalog from the colors of the PNG. Index 0 is transparent.

sprpanel.extract_warning.text: If this palette already exists, its colors are replaced.

sprsheet.edit_tip.text: Opens the source PNG in the configured image editor.

comped.pivot_x_tip.text: Sets the horizontal position of the pivot, in pixels from the centre of the sprite frame. 0, 0 is the centre. Rotation, scale and flip happen around this point, and it stays fixed on screen. It does not move the sprite: the offset does.

comped.pivot_y_tip.text: Sets the vertical position of the pivot, in pixels from the centre of the sprite frame. 0, 0 is the centre. Rotation, scale and flip happen around this point, and it stays fixed on screen. It does not move the sprite: the offset does.

comped.collision_blocks_tip.text: Moving actors that have a solid box are pushed out of this box instead of passing through it (a chest, an NPC, a crate). The collision map still has the last word, and the collision matrix decides which tags are stopped. Off by default.

comped.trigger_tip.text:
manual: plays nothing; call self:play_sfx() from a script.
on_spawn: plays when the actor starts.
on_destroy: plays just before the actor is destroyed.
A button or an input: plays while the actor is active and that button is held.

comped.palette_tip.text: “No palette” uses the original colors of the PNG, which is the default. Otherwise, pick one of the active palettes of the scene.

comped.anim_speed_tip.text: Sets the number of GBA ticks between two frames, for the initial state ({state}) only. A tick lasts 1/60 of a second: 8 = 7.5 fps, 4 = 15 fps, 2 = 30 fps.

comped.affine_tip.text: Reserves one of the 32 affine slots for this sprite, even at identity. The sprite can then rotate and scale around the centre of its frame, and the three local settings below apply on top of the transform of the actor. Ticking the box centres the actor on the frame: the offset becomes minus half the frame size, and collision boxes still at 0, 0 follow.

comped.scale_x_tip.text: Sets the local X scale, multiplied by the scale of the actor. The sprite scales around the pivot point. A negative value mirrors it around that point.

comped.scale_y_tip.text: Sets the local Y scale, multiplied by the scale of the actor. The sprite scales around the pivot point. A negative value mirrors it around that point.

comped.rotation_tip.text: Sets the local rotation in degrees, added to the rotation of the actor.

comped.offset_x_tip.text: Sets the horizontal offset from the actor, in pixels. The sprite is drawn at the position of the actor plus this offset, and it turns and scales with the actor.

comped.offset_y_tip.text: Sets the vertical offset from the actor, in pixels. The sprite is drawn at the position of the actor plus this offset, and it turns and scales with the actor.

comped.sfx_note.text: Sounds added from the Sound Mixer screen appear here.

comped.trigger_note.text: Every trigger except manual works without a script.

comped.palette_note.text: Active palettes are set in the scene inspector.

comped.anim_speed_note.text: Other states keep their own speed, set in the Sprite Editor.

comped.affine_note.text: When off, the rotation and scale of the actor can still be read and written from scripts, but nothing draws them.

win.oam_tip.text:
OAM is a 1 KiB memory holding 128 sprite entries (OBJ). Each entry holds the position, size and appearance of one hardware sprite.
Counted here: the entries the build reserves for the active scene. These are its active actors that have a sprite, shown or hidden, its sprite-target interface zones and its prefab pools.

win.oam_note.text: An actor without a sprite uses no entry. Entries beyond 128 are not drawn, and the build refuses the scene.

win.cycles_tip.text:
The GBA has 1210 cycles per scanline to draw sprites. A regular sprite costs about its width in pixels. A rotated or scaled sprite costs twice its width plus 10.
Counted here: the busiest of the 160 lines of the active scene, from the sprites shown at scene start and the sprite-target text zones.

win.cycles_note.text: Beyond the budget, the sprites that come later in OAM order are not drawn on that line.

win.vram_tip.text:
VRAM is 96 KiB: 64 KiB for backgrounds, then a 32 KiB area for sprite graphics. That area holds 1024 tiles of 8×8 pixels in 4bpp, or 512 when a scene uses a bitmap mode.
Counted here: every frame of every sprite the ROM loads, once per sprite, plus the tiles of sprite-target text zones. A 16×16 sprite takes 4 tiles per frame and a 32×32 sprite takes 16.

win.vram_note.text: This count covers the whole project, not only the active scene: sprites stay resident while the game runs.

win.objpal_tip.text:
Palette RAM is 1 KiB and holds two palettes of 256 colors: one for sprites, one for backgrounds. In 4bpp, the sprite palette is cut into 16 banks of 16 colors.
Counted here: the banks the active scene occupies, from the palettes its sprites reference and the own palettes the editor places in free banks.

win.objpal_note.text: Color 0 of each bank is transparent.

win.bgpal_tip.text:
Palette RAM holds two palettes of 256 colors: one for backgrounds, one for sprites. In 4bpp, the background palette is cut into 16 banks of 16 colors.
Counted here: the banks the active scene occupies, from its background layers and its interface text.

win.bgpal_note.text: Color 0 of each bank is transparent.

win.sram_tip.text:
The cartridge keeps saves in 32 KiB of battery-backed SRAM.
Counted here: the save slots times the size of one slot, which holds the persistent global variables. The count stays at 0 while no variable is persistent.

win.sram_note.text: This count covers the whole project, not only the active scene. Beyond 32 KiB, the build is refused.

win.ewram_tip.text:
EWRAM is 256 KiB of work RAM, slower than IWRAM (16-bit bus), reserved at startup. The engine keeps its actor and sprite tables and the script state there, and allocates nothing during play.
Counted here: the static data the linker places in EWRAM.

win.iwram_tip.text:
IWRAM is 32 KiB of fast work RAM (32-bit bus), reserved at startup. The stack grows down from its top, so the more data is stored from the bottom, the less room the stack has.
Counted here: the static data and code the linker places in IWRAM.

win.iwram_part_iwram.text: Engine routines placed in fast memory

win.after_build_note.text: The value is known after a build.

win.affine_tip.text:
The GBA has 32 affine matrices. A sprite that rotates or scales uses one.
Counted here: the matrices the active scene requests with Affine transform, one per actor that enables it and one per actor of each prefab pool whose root enables it.

win.affine_note.text: A child actor without its own rotation or scale shares its parent's matrix at no cost. A request beyond 32 gets no matrix, and its sprite is drawn without the transform.

win.bgvram_tip.text:
The first 64 KiB of VRAM hold background graphics, in 4 charblocks of 16 KiB. Tiles and tilemaps share this space, in blocks of 2 KiB.
Counted here: the blocks the active scene uses for its background tiles, their tilemaps and the glyphs of its interface text.

win.bgvram_note.text: A scene whose backgrounds do not fit is refused by the build.

win.iwram_note.text: The stack is not counted: it needs free space at the top of IWRAM.

akind.add_palette_tip.text: Opens a menu to create a 16-color or 256-color palette, or to import one.

akind.font_source_tip.text: {value} glyphs of {cell_w}×{cell_h} px, {value_2} tiles in the charblock of the UI layer.

palgrid.export_tip.text: Exports the palette as a .gpl (GIMP) file, a .pal (JASC) file or a hex list.

palgrid.empty.text: Select a palette from the left panel

colins.snap_tip.text: The color is snapped to the GBA's 15-bit grid, with 5 bits per channel.

paluse.open_tip.text: {detail}. Opens this item in its editor.

fontinsp.bg_tip.text: Makes this sheet color transparent. The flat background color is chosen when the sheet was imported without alpha.

fontinsp.space_tip.text: Makes this spacing marker transparent so it does not appear in the game.

fontinsp.charset_tip.text: Lists the characters covered by this font. Editing it assigns characters to glyph cells in order.

fontinsp.charset_hint.text: Editing reassigns characters to cells in order. Extra cells keep their character; ligatures are set cell by cell.

fontinsp.char_tip.text: Assigns one or more characters to this glyph. Multiple characters create a ligature.

fontinsp.glyph_hint.text: Glyphs are drawn in the image editor, just like for a sprite. Here only the character each cell corresponds to is corrected.

fontinsp.key_none.text: No transparent color. The sheet is used as-is.

fontinsp.key_count.singular: {n} color made transparent. The PNG is not modified.
fontinsp.key_count.plural: {n} colors made transparent. The PNG is not modified.

fontinsp.adv_mono.text: Mono advance. Designating the spacing makes it proportional.

glsheet.hint_default.text: A click on a cell, then typing, assigns the character it represents. The selection advances on its own. The arrow keys navigate.

glsheet.merge_tip.text: Merges the selected cells into one glyph covering their rectangle.

glsheet.pick_hint.text: A click on the sheet picks the {name} color (Escape cancels).

mktool.wraps.text: Wraps the selection; a second click removes it.

mktool.dropped.text: Is inserted in front of the selection, which is left intact.

mktool.value_tip.text: Inserts the value of a project global or constant, read at display time.

txtinsp.empty.text:
Select a text entry
from the table

txtinsp.note_tip.text: Holds context useful for translation. This note is never shown in the game.

txttbl.empty_tip.text: Shows only the entries with no content yet.

txttbl.unused_tip.text: Shows only the entries that no script and no layout refers to.

txttbl.missing_tip.text: Shows only the entries without a translation in the active language.

txttbl.group_rename_tip.text: A selected and expanded filing is renamed by clicking its label; this renames the filing of every text it contains.

txttbl.used_unknown_tip.text: Scripts could not be parsed. Usage is unknown, not zero.

txttbl.unused_cell_tip.text: No script and no layout refers to this key.

txtwb.copy_tip.text: Copies the key, to paste into a Lua script.

txtwb.filing_tip.text: Organizes the table and suggests a key without changing a defined key.

txtwb.preview_font_tip.text: Chooses the font of the preview without changing the text.

uielemname.taken_msg.text:
An interface element named “{name}” already exists (in “{interface}”). Element names are unique in the whole project, because scripts cite them with interface:get.

Yes: use “{suggested}” instead.
No: keep the current name and choose another one.

uiinsp.size_fixed_image.text: An image takes the size of its sprite frame: the hardware cannot stretch it.

uiinsp.size_fixed_text.text: A Text string is placed at a point and its width is a build detail. To choose a width, use a Textbox.

txtlib.add_text.text: Add a text in the selected folder

txtpnl.invalid_key_msg.text: “{name}” is empty or already used by another text.

txtpnl.empty_sequence_msg.text:
“{page}” is the only text of a sequence that a table or a TextBox follows. Renaming it to “{name}” takes it out of the sequence: the linked table loses its row (undo restores it) and the TextBox is left empty.

Rename anyway?

txtpnl.delete_msg.text:
Delete {what}?

Scripts that use them will no longer compile.

txtscr.reslice_confirm_msg.text:
Re-slice “{name}” into {cw}×{ch} cells?

Assigned characters are reset from scratch. Manual corrections will be lost.

backdrop.tip.text: Cycles through the proof backgrounds: the current one is {name}, the next one is {next}.

scrsb.bg_ref.text: Editorial reference. A background is placed in the scene, not from a script.

vartbl.array_tip.text: Sets the number of cells of the array, indexed from 1 (global.name[1]..[N]).

vartbl.array_note.text: A right-click then Array turns it back into a single value.

palslot.slot_tip.text: Uses palette {name}; a click replaces it and a right-click removes it.

palslot.override_tip.text: {names} uses {tgt} instead of its original palette. A click changes it; a right-click restores the original palette.

palslot.add_palette_tip.text: Adds a palette from the project catalog to this sprite.

palslot.compressed_tip.text: {names} uses a fixed palette{span_txt}. It cannot be remapped.

palslot.own_palette_tip.text: {names} uses its own palette. A click overrides it with a project palette.

pick.pick_hint.text: Picks a color from the bank this text reads.

pick.index_tip.text: Index {_index} of the bank. The color code is shown, not typed.

pick.stale_index_tip.text: This index is kept, but the bank this text reads has no such color. Nothing will be painted with it.

rombar.mode_tip.text: Fill shows the free cartridge space; breakdown compares the resource categories.

projpick.add_personal_hint.text:
Personal presets are added as folders in:
{USER_STARTERS_DIR}

cvregion.region_tip.text:
{name}, in the interface {layout}.
{tiles}Target: {target}.
Dragging moves it, the handles resize it, Alt-drag duplicates it.

cvtool.collision_editing_tip.text: Paints collision cells on the active scene with the chosen brush.

cvtool.scene_inpainting_tip.text: Recolors the palette assigned to the background tiles of the scene with the chosen tool.

cvtool.interface_widget_tip.text: Places an interface element of the chosen type by dragging its area on the canvas.

bglayer.reorder_tip.text: Dragging onto another layer swaps their display priority.

bglayer.image_tip.text: A click chooses a PNG; a PNG can also be dropped here.

bglayer.inpaint_title.text: Repaint the palettes of this layer

bglayer.visibility_title.text: Show or hide this layer on the canvas

actorinsp.expose_warning.text: Every other instance is updated too.

actorinsp.expose_new_title.text: Create a prefab from this actor

actorinsp.parent_note.text: This is not inheritance: to reuse a definition, use a prefab. The parent must be in the same scene, and a cycle is refused at build.

bglayer.no_palette_tip.text: Uses the colors of the PNG.

caminsp.starting_camera_tip.text: Sets which of the cameras of this scene is active when the scene starts. A script can switch to another with camera.switch.

caminsp.actor_local_note.text: Actor names are local to a scene: a camera reused in a scene without that actor simply stays still there.

caminsp.prefill_tip.text: Prefills the width and height from the background of the selected scene whose parallax speed is closest to 1.0.

caminsp.no_background.text: This scene has no background placed.

dyninsp.empty.text:
Select a scene
or an actor to
show its properties

inputs.hint.text: Name an action and choose the buttons that must be held together. Use it in scripts with input:held("name"), input:pressed("name"), input:released("name"), input:buffered("name", frames). The arrows are the D-pad axes.

inputs.interact_locked.text: Built-in input of the Interactive component: it exists in every project, its name is fixed and it cannot be removed. Only its buttons are yours to choose (A by default). Scripts can read it too: input:pressed("interact").

inputs.interact_reach_tip.text: How far, in pixels, the box of the player is projected in the direction it looks to reach an Interactive actor (Facing mode). Walls stop it.

langcard.source_note.text: The source language lives in texts.json. Each translation gets its own assets/texts_<code>.json.

langcard.code_tip.text: Names the translation file, for example texts_de.json.

langcard.name_tip.text: Readable name, shown in the editor and, when it exists, in the language menu of the game.

langcard.this_project_has_no_font_yet.text: This project has no font yet.

projinsp.start_scene_tip.text: First scene loaded when the ROM boots.

projinsp.empty.text: Select a scene or an actor in the left panel to show its properties.

projset.save_slots_tip.text: Sets how many separate saves the game can hold in SRAM. Scripts address them by number: save:write(0).

projset.cartridge_tip.text: Sets the capacity the build report compares the ROM against. The sizes are the ones actually manufactured for the GBA.

projset.debug_tip.text: Enables debug.* in scripts: debug:log(...) writes to the mGBA log console, and the engine measures frame time, OAM usage, sound channels and DMA load once per frame.

projset.backdrop_tip.text: Sets index 0 of the BG palette. It is shown wherever no layer or sprite draws, including through a window that masks everything.

projset.transition_tip.text: Fade played when the game leaves a scene and when it opens one. Each scene fades out with its own setting and fades in with the setting of the scene being opened, including the first scene.

projset.frames_tip.text: Sets the duration of each half of the transition, in frames. 16 frames is a bit over a quarter of a second.

projset.rate_tip.text: Effects are converted to 8-bit mono but keep their sample rate, so a 44.1 kHz effect costs about three times what it would at 16 kHz.

projset.channels_tip.text: Sets the number of software mixing channels, shared by music and sound effects. A module needs one per voice, and every effect playing takes one more. Sound effect references follow a separate limit of {handle_slots}: a further effect still plays, but has no reference.

projset.default_font_tip.text: Fills coverage holes: a character missing from the active font, such as a Latin word left untranslated under a Japanese font, or any glyph missing from the font of the scene.

projinsp.start_scene_note.text: It is independent of the scene open in the editor.

projset.backdrop_note.text: Every scene that does not set its own backdrop inherits it. The value is quantized to the GBA’s BGR555 color format.

projset.cartridge_note.text: Going over the capacity is reported as an error. The ROM is still built, but it does not fit on that cartridge.

projset.channels_note.text: Each channel costs {channel_bytes} bytes of heap, plus a fixed {buffer_bytes}-byte mixing buffer. Eight channels, the default, cost {default_bytes} bytes.

projset.debug_note.text: When unchecked (Release), every debug.* call and the measurement it costs are removed at compile time, not just silenced.

projset.default_font_note.text: A character missing from both fonts is still reported. With no default font, a missing glyph is simply skipped and draws nothing.

projset.rate_title.text: Default sample rate for sound effects

projset.rate_note.text: Resampling happens at build time. The file in assets/ is never rewritten, so raising the rate again loses nothing.

projset.save_slots_note.text: Only the global variables marked persist are stored. A project with none writes no save data at all.

projset.transition_note.text: While a transition plays, the outgoing scene is frozen and its own color blending is suspended: there is no fade on top of a translucency.

scrinsp.empty.text:
Select a script
from the left panel

scrinsp.remove_var_confirm.text: Remove the exposed variable '{name}' from the script?

dirwidget.direction_tip.text: Creates or edits the frames played when the actor faces this direction.

dirwidget.mirror_h_tip.text: Generates the W, NW and SW directions from E, NE and SE.

dirwidget.mirror_v_tip.text: Generates the S, SE and SW directions from N, NE and NW.

spritelibrary.add_state_tip.text: Creates a new animation state with its own directions, speed, and loop setting.

spritelibrary.animation_tree_tip.text: A direction selected here is edited in the frame canvas. **F2** *renames the selected animation state* (so does a second click on it); a right-click offers renaming and deletion.

fontinsp.merge_stats.text:
{count} cells selected
merge → one {value}×{value_2} glyph ({tw}×{th} tiles)

bginp.edit_image_tip.text: Opens the source PNG in the configured image editor. A right-click offers another editor.

bginp.select_tip.text: Places the image in its canvas. The whole file is shown, dimmed where it falls outside the canvas. Dragging the image moves it; the handles scale it. Shift keeps the proportions, Ctrl snaps to 8 px. Choosing another tool applies, Esc cancels. The image file is never changed.

bgedit.canvas_fit_tip.text: Fits the whole image inside the canvas, centered.

bgedit.canvas_fill_tip.text: Covers the whole canvas; what overflows is cropped.

bgedit.canvas_one_to_one_tip.text: Shows the image at its file size, centered.

bginp.passe_partout_tip.text: How much the area outside the canvas is dimmed. At 0 what overflows shows as it is.

bginp.paint_needs_palette.text: No added palette: “+” in the palettes grid adds one

bgedit.canvas_fixed_tip.text: A bitmap background is a full-screen 240×160 buffer (Mode 4), so its canvas cannot change. The tiled layout allows any size.

hints.bg.canvas_move.text: Moves the image, or scales it by its handles

bginp.mirror_x_tip.text: Adds a vertical bar. The left side is mirrored onto the right; dragging the arrow handle across the bar keeps the right side instead. Ctrl snaps to 8 px. Applied before compression, so it can change the tile count. The image file is never changed.

bginp.mirror_y_tip.text: Adds a horizontal bar. The top side is mirrored onto the bottom; dragging the arrow handle across the bar keeps the bottom side instead. Ctrl snaps to 8 px. Applied before compression, so it can change the tile count. The image file is never changed.

bginp.prep_reset_tip.text: Cancels the crop, resize and mirror adjustments.

bgedit.analyze_tip.text: Measures the colors per tile, shared colors and required palettes.

bgedit.comp_toggle_tip.text: Shows the settings that reduce the image to what the GBA accepts. It opens by itself when the image does not fit as it is.

bgedit.save_png_tip.text: Bakes the painting and the palette repaints into a PNG in the project's assets, and makes it the source of this background. The palettes keep their banks (indexed PNG, 16 colors per bank). The old source file is left untouched.

bgedit.save_png_confirm.text:
Save this background as a PNG?
The painting and the palette repaints are baked into the image, which becomes its source.

bgedit.save_png_failed.text: The saved PNG did not read back identically. Nothing was changed.

bgedit.export_png_tip.text: Saves the image as it is displayed to a PNG file of your choice. The background itself is not changed.

akind.relink_warn_background.text:
Relinking re-imports the image: its crop, size and compression settings are reset, and its color mode is detected again. The painting and the palette repaints are kept.
Relink anyway?

akind.relink_warn_image.text:
Relinking re-imports the image: what was derived from the old file (palettes, tiles) is computed again.
Relink anyway?

bgedit.adj_toggle_tip.text: Shows the settings that change the colors of the image before compression. They open by themselves when an adjustment is set.

bgedit.adj_hue_tip.text: Rotates the colors around the color wheel, in degrees.

bgedit.adj_saturation_tip.text: Makes the colors more or less vivid. At the minimum the image is gray.

bgedit.adj_brightness_tip.text: Lightens or darkens the whole image.

bgedit.adj_contrast_tip.text: Widens or narrows the gap between light and dark areas.

bgedit.adj_reset_tip.text: Puts hue, saturation, brightness and contrast back to neutral.

bgedit.dither_kind_tip.text: How the color reduction spreads its error. Diffusion follows the image; ordered patterns are regular, so they tile cleanly.

bgedit.dithering_needs_global.text: Needs « Global colors » above Off: without a first color reduction there is no error to spread.

bgedit.comp_palettes_tip.text: Sets how many of the 16 sub-palettes the image may use. Fewer palettes give fewer distinct colors.

bgedit.comp_colors_tip.text: Sets the colors in each sub-palette. Index 0 stays transparent. Fewer colors give a flatter, more graphic result.

bgedit.comp_global_tip.text: Reduces the whole image to this many colors before it is cut into tiles, so neighbouring tiles share their colors. When off, tiles are reduced separately.

bgedit.comp_tiles_tip.text: Limits the number of tiles kept. Similar tiles are merged when the limit is exceeded, starting with the most uniform areas.

bgedit.comp_tiles_tip_note.text: Hardware limit: 512 tiles in 4bpp or 256 tiles in 8bpp per charblock.

bgedit.comp_method_tip.text: How colors are merged inside a tile that has too many.

bgedit.comp_colors8_tip.text: Sets the colors in the single 256-color palette. Index 0 stays transparent. Fewer colors give a flatter, more graphic result and make more neighbouring tiles merge.

langcard.remove_tip.text: Its translation file is kept on disk.

caminsp.starting_camera_note.text: This choice does not depend on the camera shown above. (none) keeps the view fixed at the origin, with no bounds and no target.

langcard.code_note.text: The code is lowercased and stripped of any character a filename refuses.

langcard.font_note.text: Only a different writing system needs one.

projset.remove_tag_used.singular: {n} box uses it and falls back to “body”.
projset.remove_tag_used.plural: {n} boxes use it and fall back to “body”.

scncanvas.bitmap_in_tiled_mode.text: Bitmap background {names}: not shown in video mode {mode}. Use mode 3, 4 or 5.

scncanvas.view_scene_tip.text: Edits the active scene on the canvas.

scncanvas.view_graph_tip.text: Shows the transitions between all scenes.

scncanvas.graph_show_notes_tip.text: Shows or hides the free notes of the graph.

scncanvas.graph_search_tip.text: Opens a field for finding a scene in the graph.

scncanvas.graph_rearrange_tip_warning.text: Manual positions are replaced and cannot be undone.

scncanvas.graph_preview_tip.text: Shows or hides the background preview of this scene on its node.

scncanvas.graph_entry_unreachable.text: Entry — unreachable scene (nothing switches to it)

scncanvas.graph_exit_dynamic.text: Exit — computed target (variable): can't be resolved, check the script

scncanvas.graph_exit_broken.text: Exit — target not found (switches to a name no scene has)

scncanvas.graph_exit_none.text: Dead end — no exit (this scene never switches away)

scncanvas.graph_delete_folder_content_co.text: Delete this folder and its {count} scene(s)? The scenes are removed (Ctrl+Z to undo each).

scncanvas.graph_delete_selection_confirm.text: Delete the selection: {scenes} scene(s) and {folders} folder(s)? Folders keep their contents; scenes are removed (Ctrl+Z).

scncanvas.grid_cycle_tip.text: A click moves to the next state: no grid, 8 px grid, 16 px grid, then back to no grid.

scncanvas.grid_8px_tip.text: Shows the 8×8 pixel boundaries of GBA tiles.

scncanvas.grid_16px_tip.text: Shows a 16×16 pixel grid for aligning sprites and scene elements.

scncanvas.snap_tip.text: Aligns actors and interface elements to the active grid while moving them.

scncanvas.actor_boxes_tip.text: Shows the collision boxes of every actor in the active scene.

scncanvas.clear_collision_tip.text: Empties the whole collision map of the active scene. **Ctrl+Z** *brings it back.*

scncanvas.collision_already_empty.text: The collision map is already empty.

scncanvas.collisions_tip.text: Shows the collision map painted for the active scene.

scncanvas.interface_tip.text: Shows text, containers, lists, and images placed in the scene.

bginp.brush_tip.text: Repaints the palette of each 8×8 tile crossed. The image pixels are not changed.

bginp.tile_brush_tip.text: Paints the selected color of the palette over each 8×8 cell crossed. Right-click restores the original tile.

bginp.tile_brush_size_tip.text: Paints a {size}×{size} px square aligned to the tile grid.

bginp.mode_inpaint_tip.text: Repaints the palette of the tiles crossed. The tiles themselves are not changed. Right-click restores the original palette.

bginp.mode_paint_tip.text: Paints a layer over the image: a solid tile of the selected color in each cell crossed. Right-click restores the original tile.

bginp.fill_tip_paint.text: Fills a contiguous area of identical cells with the selected color.

bginp.rectangle_tip_paint.text: Puts the selected color in every cell of a rectangular area.

bginp.eraser_tip_paint.text: Removes both the palette repaint and the painted color of each 8×8 cell crossed: the original tile and palette come back.

hints.bg.fill_tiles.text: Fills the connected cells with the selected color

hints.bg.paint_rect_tiles.text: Paints a rectangle with the selected color

hints.bg.erase_all.text: Restores the original tiles and palettes

bginp.run_encoding_tip.text: Encodes the settings shown now, even when the background is up to date or the encoding is slow.

bginp.adjust_preview.text: Preview — not the GBA render yet

bginp.fill_tip.text: Repaints the palette of a contiguous area of tiles. The image pixels are not changed.

bginp.rectangle_tip.text: Repaints the palette of every tile in a rectangular area. The image pixels are not changed.

bginp.eraser_tip.text: Removes both the palette repaint and the painted color of each 8×8 cell crossed: the original tile and palette come back.

bginp.grid_tip.text: Shows the 8×8 pixel grid used by GBA tiles.

uses.no_instance_in_the_project.text: Not placed or spawned anywhere in the project.

txtinsp.usage_unknown.text: scripts could not be parsed (usage unknown)

scttree.iface_shared_note.text: Editing it affects all of them.

uiinsp.bank_inherited_note.text: It is changed through the fill of the container.

uiinsp.priority.note.text: 0 is frontmost and 3 is backmost; a number overrides the actor.

uiinsp.text.bank_note.text: One more bank would cost one more copy of the glyphs in VRAM. This is also the Scene inspector setting: changing it here changes it for the whole scene.

uiinsp.text.ink_note.text: Each color used costs one more copy of the glyphs in VRAM.

uiinsp.text.highlight_note.text: Composing costs a block of surface tiles for the scene, whatever the font. A background or a highlight both pay it once.

uiinsp.fill.sprite_note.text: It costs one sprite per cell, because a sprite cannot be stretched.

uiinsp.fill.state_note.text: A script can change it later by writing the image state: interface:get("name").state = "state".

uiinsp.fill.speed_note.text: That value stays the single source of truth: otherwise, fixing a speed there would silently stop having any effect here.

uiinsp.list.selection_note.text: That lets a menu and its submenu show at once; without it, both would walk on the same press. Hiding the list is different: it disappears.

uiinsp.list.columns_note.text: Scrolling moves by a whole line, so the columns an author laid out stay where they are.

uiinsp.list.order_note.text: With a single column both describe the same walk; the other axis of the D-pad is then left to the game.

uiinsp.list.ink_note.text: Each color costs one more copy of the glyphs in VRAM.

uiinsp.img.state_note.text: A script can switch to any other state of this sprite: interface:get("name").state = "state".

cvitems.camera_tip.text:
GBA camera {name}: {w}×{h} px.
Dragging moves the view.

cvtool.select_tip.text: Selects and moves actors or interface elements on the canvas.

cvtool.add_actor_tip.text: A click on the canvas places a new actor.

cvtool.eraser_tip.text: A click on an actor removes it from the active scene.

cvtool.collision_brush_8_8_px.text: Paints collision cells one 8×8 pixel tile at a time.

cvtool.collision_brush_16_16_px.text: Paints collision cells in 16×16 pixel blocks.

cvtool.floor_slope_triangle_bresenham.text: Paints a rising floor slope as a triangle.

cvtool.ceiling_slope_tip.text: Paints an inverted floor slope as a triangle.

cvtool.inpaint_brush_tip.text: Repaints the palette of each 8×8 tile crossed. The image pixels are not changed.

cvtool.inpaint_rect_tip.text: Repaints the palette of every tile in a rectangular area. The image pixels are not changed.

cvtool.text_tip.text: Places a text string at a point. It never wraps. Its content is written here, or left empty for a script to fill.

cvtool.textbox_tip.text: Creates a text box. The text wraps and aligns inside its rectangle.

cvtool.container_tip.text: Creates a parent area for grouping elements. It can anchor children and draw a background.

cvtool.image_tip.text: Creates an image element. A script can switch the state of its sprite.

bglayer.no_blend_tip.text: Takes no part in the blend; a click makes it the top layer.

bglayer.top_tip.text: This layer is the one that gets blended.

bglayer.bottom_tip.text: The top layer blends with this layer, which sits behind it.

cvtop.cursor_unit_tip.text: Shown in pixels or in 8 px tiles. **Click** *switches the unit in every canvas.*

bgedit.bitmap_needs_tiles.text: ⚠ Bitmap (Mode 4). A {value} needs tiles; switch to Tiled.

bgedit.w_h_px_not_a_multiple_of_8.text: ⚠ {w}×{h} px not a multiple of 8. Padded with transparency ({value}×{value_2}).

bgedit.iw_ih_not_divisible_by_fw_fh_valu.text: ⚠ {iw}×{ih} not divisible by {fw}×{fh}. {value}×{value_2} px left out.

boxplay.no_transition.text: No transition from “{_current}” to “{state_name}”: the ROM would not change music here.

txtinsp.no_glyph.text: “{name}” has no glyph “{value}”. Merge the cells that draw it and give it that name.

txtinsp.tiles_no_color.text: “{name}” is rendered in tiles: “[color]” will be ignored there (it requires a composed font, proportional, or too large for VRAM).

txtinsp.unknown_value.text: “${value}” is neither a project global nor a constant.

bglayer.through_tip.text: This layer is seen through; a click puts it behind instead.

bglayer.behind_tip.text: Sits behind the translucent layer; a click makes it the translucent one.

inputs.sequences_hint.text: A named sequence recognized by input:get_sequence("name"): a quarter-circle, a half-circle, a dragon punch, or a composition of its own. Its expression uses "+" for a chord (down + a), "-" for the next step (down - down+right - right) and "(a|b)" for either.

inputs.window_tip.text: Sets how many frames may pass between two steps of this sequence.

inputs.axes_hint.text: Declares a scalar axis: it remaps the D-pad, or drives one with other buttons or actions. "horizontal" and "vertical" (the D-pad) always exist, even in a project that declares none.

langcard.no_font_replacement.text: No font replacement: this language uses the fonts of the project.

caminsp.windows_over_budget.text: {used} / {total} windows used by this scene. Over budget, build will fail

bgedit.margin_rounding.text: ⚠ Margin {margins} is not a multiple of 8. Rounded down to the tile at build.

akind.no_font_assets.text: Create a font asset, then configure its sources and rendering recipe.

akind.font_asset_tip.text: Pixel height {pixel_height} px, line height {line_height} px.

fontasset.preview_text_placeholder.text: Type a sample, using Enter for line breaks

fontasset.preview_text_tip.text: This text is only used by the preview. Line breaks reveal the actual line height.

fontasset.preview_size_tip.text: Shared with the inspector and saved in this font asset.

fontasset.preview_size_fixed_tip.text: Size is fixed by the imported bitmap sheet: unlike a vector font, it cannot be rasterized at another size.

fontasset.preview_canvas_tip.text: Compares the source font with its rasterized result. The grid marks 8×8 GBA tiles.

fontasset.preview_ink_loss.text: Only {kept}% of source ink survives this output. Try a larger pixel height, a lower threshold than {threshold}, or dithering.

fontasset.preview_summary.text: {pixel_height} px · line height {line_height} px · {pixel_fit} pixel fit · {hinting} hinting · {raster_mode} · {sources}

crash.intro.text: The editor hit an unexpected error. Your saved files are untouched. You can keep working, but saving again soon is a good idea.

sndmix.add_action_tip.text: Creates an action that animation frames can trigger.

sndmix.add_state_tip.text: Creates a new state with its own sound assignments.

sndmix.remove_state_tip.text: Removes the selected column and its sound assignments.

sndmix.matrix_target_tip.text: Chooses what action “{action}” plays in state “{state}”.

sndmix.source_tip.text: Chooses whether this transition starts from this state or from any state.

sndmix.loop_tip.text: Restarts the track after its last pattern while this state remains active.

sndmix.add_transition_tip.text: Creates a transition from the selected state.

sndpanel.new_box_tip.text: Creates a new box in this sound family.

sndpanel.delete_box_warning.text: The box and its states are removed from the project.

sndpanel.preview_volume_tip.text: Changes the editor preview volume only. It does not change the asset.

sndbar.channels_tip.text: Shows the highest combined channel count of the MusicBox and JingleBox being edited.

sndbar.channels_note.text: Sound effects are not counted because their simultaneous use cannot be predicted.

txtinsp.markup_tip.text: Shows the markup used by the selected text and any validation issues.

txtwb.key_tip.text: The key written in scripts. Renaming it updates the scripts that reference it.

fontasset.primary_tip.text: Uses this source first for the regular face.

fontasset.fallbacks_tip.text: Uses these sources in order when the primary source does not cover a character.

fontasset.pixel_height_tip.text: Sets the rasterized height for vector sources.

fontasset.line_height_tip.text: Sets the vertical distance between two lines in the game.

fontasset.pixel_fit_tip.text: Chooses how the rasterizer aligns the source to the pixel grid.

fontasset.hinting_tip.text: Chooses how vector outlines are adjusted at small sizes.

fontasset.raster_mode_tip.text: Chooses how pixel coverage is encoded for the GBA output.

fontasset.threshold_tip.text: Sets the coverage level required to keep a pixel in binary or dithered output.

fontasset.dither_tip.text: Chooses the pattern used by dithered output.

fontasset.offset_x_tip.text: Shifts the rasterized glyphs horizontally without changing the source.

fontasset.offset_y_tip.text: Shifts the rasterized glyphs vertically without changing the source.

fontasset.prefer_bitmap_strike_tip.text: Uses an embedded bitmap size when the source provides one.

glsheet.reslice_tip.text: Cuts the sheet again with the selected cell size.

txttbl.rename_group_key.text: Rename all keys in this group, keeping their numbers

scred.back_tip.text: Returns to the previous screen after saving pending changes.

scred.new_script_tip.text: Creates an empty Lua script in the project.

scred.completion_tip.text: Shows the API, project names and Lua keywords available at the cursor.

scrsb.filter_tip.text: Filters events, API entries and project references by name.

scrsb.event_tip_note.text: Selecting inserts this handler, or jumps to it when it already exists.

scrsb.behavior_stub_tip.text: Inserts an exported function for this behavior module.

vartbl.rename_tip.text: Renames this variable and updates its references in scripts and text.

vartbl.type_int_tip.text: Whole number from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 (32 bits). The general-purpose type.

vartbl.type_bool_tip.text: True or false (0 or 1). Takes one byte in memory and a single bit in a save.

vartbl.type_u8_tip.text: Whole number from 0 to 255 (8 bits, no sign). Wraps around past the limits.

vartbl.type_u16_tip.text: Whole number from 0 to 65,535 (16 bits, no sign). Wraps around past the limits.

vartbl.type_s8_tip.text: Whole number from -128 to 127 (8 bits, signed). Wraps around past the limits.

vartbl.type_s16_tip.text: Whole number from -32,768 to 32,767 (16 bits, signed). Wraps around past the limits.

vartbl.type_string_tip.text: Text shown by text.draw. Held in the game as an entry of the text table, so it can be drawn and compared but not edited character by character.

vartbl.type_string_note.text: A global of this type cannot be saved.

vartbl.string_value_tip.text: The text, or the key of an existing text of the project.

datagrid.add_column_tip.text: Adds an integer column to this table.

datagrid.column_tip.text: A double-click on a name renames it. A right-click changes its type or removes it.

datainsp.type_tip.text: Controls the values accepted by this column. Changing it clears the existing values (Undo restores them).

colins.hex_tip.text: Takes a six-digit RGB color and converts it to the GBA’s 15-bit color format.

fontselect.weight_tip.text: Uses an available native face of the selected font.

backdrop.note.text: Reading aid only. It does not change the text or the ROM.

build.refresh_tip.text: Runs the checks again and updates this list.

disk.refresh_tip.text: Reads the assets folder again and updates this tree.

disk.up_tip.text: Goes back to the parent folder.

akind.relink_none.text: No compatible file in the project.

disk.open_assets_tip.text: Opens the assets folder in the file explorer.

assetlibrary.locate_tip.text: Shows the file of this asset in the Disk tab.

disk.add_folder_tip.text: Adds to the selected folder: import a file, create an asset, or make a folder.

disk.rename_refused.text: The item was not renamed: the name is empty, uses a forbidden character or is already taken, or the item is a project table.

disk.deleted.singular: Deleted {n} asset. Ctrl+Z undoes; its source file stays.
disk.deleted.plural: Deleted {n} assets. Ctrl+Z undoes; their source files stay.

disk.plus_tip.text: Adds to the folder shown: import a file, create an asset, or make a folder.

disk.create_named_tip.text: Makes an asset of this type from the selected source file, next to it.

disk.create_other_tip.text: Other asset types this file can become.

disk.create_no_common_type.text: These files cannot become the same type of asset: select sources of one format, or of formats that share a type.

disk.create_sources_only.text: Create works on source files only: leave out the folders and assets from the selection.

disk.delete_items_confirm.plural: Delete these {n} items from the disk? Ctrl+Z undoes.

disk.delete_cited.text: Cited by an asset (it will lose its source):

disk.delete_confirm.singular: Delete this asset? Its source file stays on disk. Ctrl+Z undoes.
disk.delete_confirm.plural: Delete these {n} assets? Their source files stay on disk. Ctrl+Z undoes.

disk.locate_missing.text: {name} has no file in Assets to locate.

sndedit.new_section_tip.text: Adds a section on the orders selected in the strip. Its name can be typed right away.

sndedit.new_section_tip_time.text: Adds a section after the last one, or in the middle of an empty track. Its name can be typed right away.

sndedit.loop_tip.text: The section can be played in a loop.

sndedit.default_tip.text: The section the music loops on when nothing else is asked.

sndedit.preview_section_tip.text: Plays the music from the start of the section and loops on it.

sndedit.lead_in_tip.text: A silent order added when a tracker song is converted to a module: it sets the tempo and speed, then the song restarts at order 1. It holds no note and is never heard. New sections start after it.

sndedit.cue_tip.text: {target}, played each time the music reaches {where}. Dragging the flag moves it, and a right-click changes or deletes it.

sndedit.unit_mismatch.text: These loop sections and cues were set for another kind of file. They cannot apply to this one.

sndedit.no_file.text: No file is associated with this music.

sndedit.weight_wav_tip.text: The module the build will write for this file, at the sample rate and loop set here. Amber above 1 MiB, red above 2 MiB.

sndedit.weight_estimate_tip.text: Estimate: the size of the source file. The real size is measured at the build, since the samples are shared with other tracks. Amber above 1 MiB, red above 2 MiB.

sndedit.weight_unknown_tip.text: Not known yet: a tracker module is measured at the build, since its samples are shared with other tracks.

sndedit.weight_built_tip.text: Measured at the last build. Amber above 1 MiB, red above 2 MiB.

sndedit.weight_shared_tip.text: Plus {kb} of samples shared with {n} other track(s).

sndedit.trim_tip.text: Shows, under the wave, the whole file with two handles: only the part between them goes into the ROM, and the ROM weight follows. The file itself is not modified. Sections keep their place on the sound when the handles move; one left outside is removed.

sndedit.trim_bar_tip.text: Drag a handle to keep a part of the file. Double-click keeps the whole file again.

sndedit.order_bar_tip.text: Drag a handle to play only some of the module's orders. Only the orders between the handles go into the ROM. Double-click plays the whole module again.

sndedit.mix_volume_tip.text: Volume of the music, as a percentage. Double-click resets it to 100 %.

sndedit.mix_tempo_tip.text: Speed of the music, as a percentage of the file's own; the pitch does not move. Heard as it changes. Double-click resets it to 100 %.

sndedit.mix_pitch_tip.text: Pitch of the music, as a percentage: higher also plays faster, lower slower. Heard as it changes. Double-click resets it to 100 %.

sndedit.mix_wav_tip.text: A WAV track keeps its own tempo and pitch: its sections are samples chained by the lines of a module, and changing either would make them drift apart.

sndedit.mix_jingle_tip.text: A jingle plays on the second layer of the mixer: only its volume applies.

sndedit.mix_type_tip.text: Click the value to type it. Enter applies it, within the fader's range.

sndedit.meters_tip.text: How loud each channel of the module sounds at the playhead, one bar per channel of the project: an empty bar is a free channel. A bar drawn in red is beyond the number of channels the project gives to the mixer, where the voice has nowhere to sound.

sndedit.poly_tip.text:
How many channels of the module sound at each moment, on the same time axis as the waveform. The dashed line is the number of channels the project gives to the mixer (shared with the sound effects); what rises above it is drawn in red, where the extra voices have nowhere to sound.
A channel whose volume has dropped to zero counts for nothing here.

sndedit.view_wave_tip.text: Shows the loudness of the music along its length, as the console plays it.

sndedit.view_scope_tip.text: Shows the last 30 ms of the sound being played, like an oscilloscope. A higher pitch packs more cycles into the window and a lower volume flattens the trace. While the music is stopped, a still window of the render is shown at the start handle.

sfxedit.wave_tip.text:
The two handles keep a part of the file: what lies outside them stays out of the ROM. The source file is not modified.
An effect weighs one byte per frame kept, so cutting a silent tail makes the ROM lighter.
The round handle at the bottom sets the fade out: drag it left from the end of the kept part.
Playback uses the same trim, fade and sample rate as the build. The bars on the right show the channel the effect takes among the project's; Scope shows the sound that plays.

sfxedit.start_tip.text: Start of the kept part, in milliseconds from the start of the file.

sfxedit.end_tip.text: End of the kept part, in milliseconds from the start of the file. The end of the file means no cut.

sfxedit.fade_tip.text: Makes the effect fade linearly to silence over its last frames (a frame is 1/60 s), inside the kept part. Applied to the sample when the ROM is built, so the console computes nothing; it removes the click of a cut that lands in the middle of the signal. Zero means no fade.

sfxedit.mix_volume_tip.text: Volume of the effect, as a percentage. Double-click resets it to 100 %.

sfxedit.mix_pitch_tip.text: Pitch the effect starts with, as a percentage of the pitch of its file: 100 is the file as it is, 200 one octave above, 50 one octave below. Heard at the next playback. A script call to set_pitch replaces it with an absolute value. Double-click resets it to 100 %.

sfxedit.mix_pan_tip.text: Where the effect starts in the stereo field: left, centre or right. The bar fills from the centre. A script call to set_panning replaces it for that playback. Double-click re-centres it.

sndedit.mix_pan_type_tip.text: Click to type: L 40, C, R 25, or -40 / 25. Enter applies it.

sfxedit.mix_variation_tip.text: Each time the effect starts, its pitch is drawn at random within this many percent above or below the starting pitch. Zero keeps it identical every time. Makes sounds that repeat — steps, hits, coins — feel natural. Heard at each playback. Double-click resets it to zero.

sfxedit.fade_in_tip.text: Makes the effect rise linearly from silence over its first frames (a frame is 1/60 s), inside the kept part. Applied to the sample when the ROM is built, so the console computes nothing; it removes the click of a cut that starts in the middle of the signal. Zero means no fade.

sfxedit.ab_tip.text: Plays the effect at the sample rate of its file instead of the rate the ROM will use, to hear what the lower rate costs. Only the preview changes; the build keeps the rate of the effect or of the project. Available when the two rates differ; the weight at the file's rate is shown below.

sfxedit.summary_rate.text: · {kb} KiB at the file's rate ({rate} Hz)

sfxedit.summary.text: Keeps {start}–{end} ms ({kept} of {total} ms) · {kb} KiB in ROM instead of {whole} KiB

sfxedit.summary_whole.text: Whole file · {total} ms · {kb} KiB in ROM

sndedit.wave_tip.text:
A horizontal drag moves the playhead, Shift + horizontal drag sets the tempo, a vertical drag the pitch, Shift + vertical drag the volume. The two handles at the bottom set the fade in and the fade out.
A click or a drag on the ruler places the start handle freely (Shift snaps it to the start of an order); the next playback starts from it, while a music that is playing keeps going. Nothing on the ruler starts the music.
The same settings are in the mix table and the inspector.

sndpanel.fade_in_tip.text: Time for the volume to rise when the music starts, in frames (60 per second).

sndpanel.fade_out_tip.text: Time for the volume to fall when the music stops, in frames (60 per second).

sndpanel.music_rate_tip.text: Quality of the track in the game. A lower rate makes it lighter and allows a longer track.

sndpanel.volume_tip.text: Sets the effect volume in the game.

sndpanel.loop_tip.text: Restarts the track when it reaches its end.

sndedit.reset_warning.text: Removes every loop section from this track.

langcard.run_language_tip.text: The Run button and F5 use this language in monolingual mode.

langcard.multilingual_tip.text: Build includes all translations and their replacement fonts.

langcard.monolingual_tip.text: Build includes only the chosen language. Game offers Build_<language> for each language.
